findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: When no per-client resource exists, `getResourceTypeResource(...)` is used as the fallback and passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)`. That method returns null if the schema is not supported for the server, if admin permissions are disabled for the realm, or if the 'Clients' resource is missing. The result is a NullPointerException, which surfaces as a 500 instead of a plain 'no permission' false. A null check should return false.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission may return the type resource name and evaluates every resource
findings.body: `findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` also matches the all-clients type resource, whose name is the literal "Clients" and not a client id. That string can end up in the returned set of client ids. Each resource is also evaluated separately through `root.evaluatePermission`, so the cost grows with the number of clients that have per-client resources. The type resource should be skipped, and the evaluation cost noted or reduced.

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: `getEvaluationContext` is never called, so `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext`, `AccessToken` and the helper itself are dead. `logger`, the static import `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` and the `Scope` import are also unused. This is copy-paste residue and should be removed.

findings.title: No cleanup of Clients-type resources when a client is deleted under V2
findings.body: The listener is now gated on `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ`, so under V2 `ClientRemovedEvent` does nothing. A client's per-client resource and any permissions referencing it remain in the admin-permissions resource server after the client is deleted. The orphaned resource is named by the old client id. There is no V2 cleanup path. Also, the gate changes existing V1 behaviour, because the listener previously ran whenever the V1 listener was registered, regardless of the feature flag.

findings.title: Tests mutate shared client state without restoring it
findings.body: `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and removes a default client scope, then re-adds it only as an optional scope. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles. `onAfter` removes only permissions, so this state leaks into other tests on the same realm. `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` indexes `getDefaultClientScopes().get(0)`, so results can depend on test order.

findings.title: JUnit 4 fail() used in a JUnit 5 test
findings.body: `org.junit.Assert.fail` is imported while the rest of the class and sibling tests use `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions`. Mixing in the JUnit 4 API depends on a transitive dependency and is inconsistent.
